title: Differences in Perception
paragraphs: “Guh… Damn it! You went and landed a needlessly heavy blow!”
“Ha! I wonder how long you’ll last!”
“Like I’m gonna take that! Meteor Sword!”

Takt then swung his sword at the panda, who was charging in for the follow-up attack. It looked like he was using one of Ren’s Skills, but the panda leaped over the star and delivered a heel drop to Takt.
“An attack with such half-assed aim is a waste of time!”
“Wh—… I’m not done yet!”

Slammed into the ground with a thud, Takt bounced back up and regained his footing. He switched the throwing weapon in one hand to a dagger, adopting a dual-wielding stance, and quickly closed in on the panda and Éclair, slashing at them. However, both the panda and Éclair anticipated the attack by a hair’s breadth and dodged it.
“Damn it! Hit them! Just a little more! These weapons are hard to use! I should be able to hit them!”
“Don’t blame your own inexperience on your weapons.”
Éclair coldly tripped Takt with her foot, while Panda spun around and slashed at him with her claws.
“Gah! Not yet!”
“Your lunge is too weak.”
Though Takt was down on one knee, he wasn’t giving up just yet. He created some distance, raised his sword, and hurled a dagger.
“Hundred Sword! Air Throw! Second Throw!”
Countless swords and daggers flew toward Éclair and Panda, but… as if in perfect timing, Zou used Magic to pull a boulder from the ground, hurled it at them, and smashed them to pieces.
“See? See? Your one-trick pony long-range attacks won’t get you anywhere, you know?”
“Those are some pretty weak attacks for someone wielding a Hero’s weapon. They’re not even good practice.”
“Don’t get all cocky, youuuu!”
“Hey, you guys! Since we’re here, I’ll show you what a real Zeltoble mercenary fight looks like!”
“‘‘‘Alrighty then! Big Sis!’’’”
At Panda’s call, her subordinates—who had been holding a defensive formation to keep the pigs from attacking us—sprang forward in response.
……Hey. Tiger Guy, why are you getting mixed up in this, too?
Then, just as Panda clapped her hands, she swiftly channeled Magic to make ten bamboo stalks sprout from the ground, closed in on Takt, and kicked him away.
“Gwaah! But this position—”
Just as Takt, who’d been sent flying into the bamboo with a thud, was trying to regain his footing, the bamboo shifted and, like a spring, flung him back toward Panda.
“Did you say something? Well, you seem pretty tough, at least. Then I’ll really start turning up the heat!”
Panda spun around and landed a backfist right on Takt’s face, sending him flying into a different set of bamboo stalks.
“Ughaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!?”
Of course, the bamboo flexed and sent him flying back up into the air.
“You guys! Finish him off!”
“You got it!”
“I’m so excited!”
“We’re doing this all for Big Sis and Shield Bon!”
“Pay for the crime of taking Atla and the queens hostage!”

Panda’s werewolf and tiger minions work together to attack Takt from every angle. It’s a mid-air beating, isn’t it? Just as it seemed Takt would be slammed into the ground by Tiger Guy’s aerial intercept, he leaped back, and while Panda was beating him senseless in midair, he threw a Molotov cocktail he’d produced.
“Whoops.”

With a “pop,” the fireball ignited, sending a huge pillar of flame shooting up. With the pillar of flame behind him, Panda rolled his neck as if to relieve a stiff shoulder, looking thoroughly annoyed.
“Gwaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!? Hot! Ouch! Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
Takt is screaming right now. Serves you right! Panda! Give ’em more!
“T-that kind of looks like a finishing move, doesn’t it?”
Father, who was treating the Queen, commented on the pandas’ coordinated attack.
“They look like they’re having fun.”
“That ‘Spear Hero’ guy said that if you get involved, it’s okay to grab the target and drag them into it, didn’t he?”
“It seems like it would make things more stable, but it also feels a bit like a joke.”
“Not even complaining… You’re something else, aren’t you?”
Pang and Panda brushed the debris off their hands.
“Bub!”
“Bubhee!”
It looks like Takt’s pig squad is rushing to cast healing and support Magic on him.
“Damn it… Don’t think you’ve won just because of this!　Don’t you think it’s cowardly to outnumber us like this?!”

“Hah! You’re making me laugh. After all that rampaging, you’re calling the guy who went and set the Spear Hero on us a coward? What kind of joke is that?　Or are you planning to say, ‘I’m above that’?”
The panda furrows her brow in annoyance and declares this to Takt. Seeing this, the pigs pick up Filolial-sama’s egg.
“Unfortunately, we’ve decided not to play along with threats involving Filolial-sama’s egg as a hostage. It won’t work!”
“Oink-oink! Oink!”
“Oink-oink-oink!”

Panda’s subordinates began fighting back against the pigs, carefully gauging their distance. Of course, amid the commotion, the hellish sound of Filolial-sama’s egg shattering into a thousand pieces echoed through the air.
Guuuuuuuuuuu… you hear that, youuuuuu! Panda, you better remember this!
But Rival is entirely to blame for this.
“Shut up! I’m about to go all out now! This is… the power of the champion of the Faubrey Martial Arts Tournament! Haaaaaaa!”
Takt, crouching low, closed in on Panda and swung his sword.
“Don’t you dare forget about me.”
But just then, Éclair stepped in, smoothly parrying the blow with her dagger. As they passed each other, she tripped him, and as Takt fell, she aimed her dagger at him.
“What!?”

“The Faubrey Martial Arts Tournament… I’ve heard it’s one of the world’s premier tournaments, gathering the finest fighters. But… I can tell right from the start. You won with skills like this? That’s completely ridiculous!”
Éclair looks utterly dumbfounded. She seems genuinely repulsed from the bottom of her heart.

“It seems the country of Faubrey is quite obsessed with these games, huh? If someone with skills like this can win the championship, then being the world’s greatest superpower isn’t all that impressive after all.”
Panda let out a sigh.
“Bub-boo!”

At that moment, the pig aimed its gun at the Panda, Éclair, and the Elephant and fired. The Panda, Éclair, and even the Elephant dodged the bullets as if they were nothing, knocking down the ones that seemed headed straight for us as we tended to the wounded.
“Heave-ho!”
“Bub!? Oink!”
The elephant actually picked up one of the pigs like a club, smashed the other pigs with it, and then sent them flying. What a fierce and spectacular blow.
“Boo-boo!”

Three pigs lunged at the massive elephant, but they were once again blown away by the elephant’s signature tackle. Hahaha! How pathetic! They deserve to suffer compound fractures as punishment for cracking Filolial-sama’s egg! And then die in agony! That’s what they deserve.
“D-damn it! What the hell is going on?! If we just take out the Spear Hero, aren’t the rest of them just small fry?!”
“I hate to be honest, but… with your childish antics, unless there’s a huge level difference, even we—before we met the Heroes—could’ve handled you.”
“Hmm.”
“I think you’re underestimating us a bit too much… Haha, don’t even think about moving!”
Zou bound the pig she’d blown away with earth magic, then spat out those words in full “Queen of Drama” mode.
“Hey! This isn’t what we agreed on!”
For some reason, Takt addressed Trash at this point.

“How utterly ridiculous. You weren’t listening to a word I said, were you…? To begin with, this plan involved summoning the spear alone to the Dragon Hourglass… no, even that wouldn’t work, would it?”

I recognized that plan. I believe it was from the next loop in this world. I recall turning Itsuki into a Brionac out of spite, but the next loop was the one where I stayed with Father and Melromarc. Incidentally, I heard this plan was just some half-baked idea I muttered without thinking during a dinner with the Pope, which he then decided to adopt on his own. Either way, it doesn’t seem like a strategy that Trash actually thought through seriously.

“I’ve told you this countless times. Even if you take Filolial hostage to neutralize and manipulate the Spear Hero, the success rate won’t even reach twenty percent. You lot don’t have enough power right now. You need to gain more strength,” he said.
Trash replied to Takt’s grilling with a look of annoyance. Apparently, this slapdash plan was Takt’s brainchild after all.
“It’s because you’re spouting unrealistic nonsense like ‘you can’t win unless you’re ten times your current level’! What’s with this ‘train for another ten years’ nonsense?!”

“You swore revenge, didn’t you? You said you’d make those bastards suffer hell, didn’t you? Well then, you’ll have to keep sharpening your claws—even if it means coughing up blood or slurping water from the gutter. Without that kind of determination, you won’t beat these guys.”
“Even at ten-to-one odds, we’d barely stand a chance,” Trash muttered.
“Don’t go spouting such laid-back nonsense! We’ve trained hard and powered up—we’re already at Level 500!”
“That’s exactly why I told you to hone your skills for ten years—because you’ll never win at that level. There’s no way we can beat this monster with that level of power!”

Saying that, Trash pointed at me. Father nodded, looking both convinced and impressed. It’s true that we’ve used countless enhancement methods, so even a ten-to-one advantage wouldn’t be enough against a Level 500 opponent.

However, if Level 5,000 Takt and his followers were under the command of Trash… no, the Wise King of Wisdom, it might be dangerous. In other words, it’s because Takt and that pack of pigs acted on their own that Filolial-sama has ended up in this situation! I suppose Father nodded because of how accurately you called them “Trash.”

“Takt, it seems you’ve been scheming and stockpiling power to defeat the Spear Hero and Naofumi’s group, but we’ve been working on our own plans, too. We took too long—or maybe we acted too soon. We’re half-baked. In other words, at your current level, you’re just small fry that those three knights over there can easily handle. That’s right!”
“Shut up! Don’t go spouting the same nonsense as that old geezer over there!”

“It’s precisely because I’ve been defeated once that I can say this… even enemies grow. The Demon of the Shield possesses the same power as the Spear… even if you seal the Spear, you’ll be counterattacked by the Shield—which holds equal power—and its minions. It seems you, who focused only on the Spear and underestimated the Shield, didn’t realize that.”

In short, Trash had been lying low for over ten years, planning to strike us while we slept. What sheer determination! It’s easy to imagine he was planning to solidify his power base as well. If he’d gone that far, I don’t know what would’ve become of me.

“There was a difference in our perceptions—between me and you lot… but I had it. Whether it be ten years or twenty… even if I were to fall before achieving my goal, I am resolved to carry out my revenge no matter what.”

Those words struck me as quite realistic. In fact, Trash has a history of battling Siltvelt for decades, significantly weakening its power—and, to go further, bringing about the downfall of the Hakuko race. I’m sure he really did have plans like that in mind.
“Ten years? Pfft! I just want to get this over with already!”
“Ten years is nothing compared to those who’ve died! Why can’t you understand that?!”
Trash shouted fiercely, but Takt didn’t seem to grasp it at all.
“You Eggbreaker, you can’t even last half a year! Can’t you? Can’t you?!”
“Is your desire for revenge—for the girl you loved who was killed—really so trivial that you’d try to settle it so easily?”
Father said, furrowing his brow slightly. I’ll ignore Rival’s provocation. Well, I suppose there’s a difference in patience between ten years and a few months.
“Ten years, I tell you!? Why the hell should I waste my time on a bunch of stupid, childish jerks!? If I take my time, I’ll just miss my chance!”
“In your case, you just couldn’t hold back.”
“Shut up! The folks at Shieldfreeden will be in such a bind without me that they’ll end up dying on their own anyway! Why can’t you understand that?!”

“Neither the Shield nor the Spear are incompetent. They possess such unreasonable power that they’re worshipped as gods! Takt, we intended to slay the gods, didn’t we? To destroy them while still human. It was a path so arduous that even if we devoted our entire lives to it, we couldn’t be sure we’d succeed.”
“That’s exactly why I’m saying I’ll take them down with my own power!”

“…If that’s what it takes to defeat them, then so be it. Whether it takes a thousand, ten thousand, or a hundred million—I’ll come up with as many strategies as it takes. But as things stand now, we’re operating on entirely different levels.”

Unlike Takt, Trash was thinking purely in practical terms, it seems. It’s no small feat to maintain that level of rationality even while your heart is filled with vengeance. Because I’ve decided—right this very moment… no, from this moment on—to brutally slaughter every single Takt in every world. There’s no way I could remain calm while harboring this desire for revenge.

“I thought we’d understand each other—both having had those dear to us taken from us… but that’s over now… Takt, you have no chance of winning. You’d be better off giving up and taking your own life; it’ll be a more peaceful way to go.”
Trash said this dismissively.

“Let me give you one last piece of advice. If you resort to underhanded tactics, you absolutely must win. Because if you lose, a far more gruesome fate awaits you than if you’d simply lost fair and square.”
“Yeah, I suppose so… Yeah, you’re absolutely right.”
Father nodded quietly twice. Of course! I’ll definitely make you suffer like hell. Don’t think you’ll go out as easily as you have before!
“I’ll say it again. If you don’t want to suffer any more, it’s in your best interest to kill yourself quickly.”
“You bastard! Whose side are you on?!”
“No, Aultcray is just giving you this advice as your ally…”
“So that’s it! This is the prelude to despair!”
Soon, Rival completed his Magic incantation.

“That power is the transformation into a being of darkness, the very essence of arcane magic that slays all—the means to defeat my enemy… The Dragon Emperor, who rules the world, commands! Cast that one into the Abyss…!”
Rival clenched his fist and shouted.
“Dragon Emperor: Curse Transformation!”
“O-o… O-oohhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!? Gaa—Gaga… Baa—Ba, Baa!”

Rival cast Magic on the pig in the white lab coat and the countless other pigs nearby. Suddenly, the pigs began rolling around, and before our very eyes, their forms began to shift… transforming into monsters.
“Don’t make me say it again. Gaelion bears all the responsibility.”
“S-s-stop it, aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa! Don’t you get it?! Spear! Hurry up and stop him!”
“…I… can’t move.”

In my heart, I want to save Filolial-sama’s egg right this very moment. But setting Rival aside, Yuki-chan has shown such resolve. So at the very least, I must not get in the way! As a token of resistance, I’ll devote myself to treating the Queen.
Ugh… Filolial-sama, please… just this once, please forgive me. I’ll definitely make amends. After Takt shattered Filolial-sama’s egg, he lunged at me with his sword.

“…Housing such a twisted power of the Dragon Emperor within yourself is like asking to be destroyed. In Siltvelt slang, that’s a ‘paper tiger’… Don’t underestimate the Dragon Emperor, you little lizard.”

As if completely ignoring Takt, Rival deftly dodged him and reached out to jab the chest of that pig who hadn’t cast any Magic… the pig who used to be the former representative of Shieldfreeden, if I recall correctly. It seems Takt didn’t even have time to resist Rival’s full-force thrust. This isn’t the kind of blow that leaves a gaping hole like the one Takt dealt to the Queen… it’s an attack designed to rip out his very soul.
“Ooogggghhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!?”

“Takt, let me tell you something interesting. It seems this guy said he couldn’t revive the personality of your dragon, Raildia, but given the nature of the Dragon Emperor, that’s impossible. If you think you failed to steal the Dragon Emperor’s Core Stone—which hasn’t had its personality overwritten—from Naofumi and the others, then you should understand.”
Takt furrowed his brow at Rival’s words.
“It was this guy who erased Raildia and absorbed her power.”
“What!?”

“The Aotatsu species possesses dragon-like qualities, so they might be able to do a little bit, but they’re just imitations after all. They’re nowhere near the real thing. If you think you’ve become stronger with body modifications of this caliber, it’s an insult to dragons—and to the Dragon Emperor.”
With veins bulging, Rival took a deep breath and spoke to Takt as if pitying him.
“I’ll tell you this… It was this guy who killed Raildia.”
“N-no way! That can’t be true! Nelshen was close friends with Raildia!”

“Impossible. You don’t understand a thing about a woman who wants to be someone’s number one. If ethics don’t matter, there are plenty of women who’d gladly step on others to get ahead. That’s the kind of woman Nelshen is.”
“Enough with this nonsense! Let Nelshen go!”
“There’s no way I’m letting her go here. This is the collective will of all those who have suffered under Shieldfreeden. As the representative of Shieldfreeden… I’m going to make this one suffer.”

Rival then sucked in the pig’s soul—which had been dragged out—as naturally as breathing, and swallowed it whole. With a thud, the pig’s body—the representative of Shieldfreeden—collapsed lifelessly to the ground.
“As I thought, even the soul tastes rotten. “Rejoice, Takt. I’ll make your Nelshen suffer eternal torment until it vanishes within Gaelion.”
“O-Ooogggghhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!?”
The pigs let out a scream at Rival’s outrageous act.
